payload.claim: The subset-support probe only exercises `declared[0].witness` — the first declared criterion's witness node id — and treats any `error` from that single call as proof that the repo's `tests` gate cannot filter by subset at all, converting the whole night's `witness` result to `skip` and returning immediately (lines 213-222) without ever calling `witness_gate` for the remaining criteria. In production this conflates two different causes of the same symptom: a repo-wide subset-filtering limitation (the case the docstring and acceptance criterion describe) and a single criterion's witness id being wrong (a typo, a renamed test, a moved file) — the latter is at least as likely as the former and is a bug in that one criterion, not in the repo's tests gate. Because the probe uses only index 0, one bad witness id silently discards every other declared criterion's real mutant-survivor finding for that night and reports it as `skip` — which per this project's own vocabulary means 'not a failure; nothing is wrong' — instead of the `error` that would previously have aborted the attempt and surfaced the problem. This holds in the fixtures added in tests/test_gates.py (whose synthetic `tests` script errors on *any* subset argument, so the single-sample probe happens to generalize correctly there) but does not hold once a real repo has more than one criterion and any one witness id is stale.
